picks.rationale: The Boston Red Sox are on an impressive eight-game winning streak and boast a potent offense that has averaged 8.33 runs per game over the last week. They face an Athletics team in horrendous form, having lost eight straight and batting a dismal 67 wRC+ in the last week. Red Sox starter Payton Tolle (3.30 ERA, 2.62 xERA) is in strong form, while Athletics starter Jack Perkins (6.72 ERA, 5.64 FIP) has struggled significantly, allowing 2.45 HR/9. With the Athletics also dealing with numerous key injuries, Boston is well-positioned to cover the run line at home.

The Milwaukee Brewers hold an excellent 39-21 home record this season and are in first place in the NL Central. They send Shane Drohan (3.48 ERA) to the mound, who faces Minnesota's Zebby Matthews, a right-hander with a concerning 5.22 ERA overall and a 7.33 ERA on the road. The Brewers' offense ranks fifth in baseball, while the Twins possess the fifth-worst bullpen ERA, creating a significant advantage for Milwaukee. This pitching mismatch and Milwaukee's strong home performance make the moneyline a high-confidence play.

picks.game: Houston Astros vs San Diego Padres
picks.rationale: The San Diego Padres present a strong pitching advantage with Robbie Ray (3.08 ERA, 2.02 WAR) on the mound, who has allowed just six earned runs over his last eight starts and holds a seven-game winning streak. Houston counters with Ronel Blanco (7.36 ERA), who is still building back from Tommy John surgery and has shown command issues with eight walks and five home runs allowed in limited innings. The Padres' offense has also been hot, averaging 5.6 runs over their last 20 games, and Petco Park's pitcher-friendly environment further benefits Ray.

picks.game: Detroit Tigers vs San Francisco Giants
picks.rationale: The Detroit Tigers are in excellent recent form, boasting a 5-1 record in their last six games and scoring eight or more runs in seven of their last eight outings. Their starting pitcher, Keider Montero, has been strong with an 8-6 record, 3.17 ERA, and a 1.00 WHIP, including a 2.45 ERA on the road. The San Francisco Giants, conversely, are struggling with a 1-5 record in their last six games and enter this matchup without a confirmed starting pitcher, having thinned their rotation at the trade deadline. This clear pitching and form advantage for Detroit, coupled with the Giants' uncertainty, makes the Tigers moneyline a confident pick.

picks.game: Chicago Cubs vs Kansas City Royals
picks.rationale: The Chicago Cubs are on a four-game winning streak, having scored 25 runs in those victories, and are firmly in the playoff race. They are sending newly acquired Kevin Gausman to the mound, whose 3.52 FIP suggests he has pitched better than his 4.38 ERA indicates, and he closed his Toronto tenure strong. The Kansas City Royals' offense has struggled recently, scoring three runs or fewer in three of their last four games. With the Cubs' hot offense, especially against left-handed pitching, and their strong road run line covering record (9-0 in last 9 road games after a win), they are well-positioned to cover the spread against Daniel Lynch IV.

New England Revolution boasts an impressive home record this season, securing 7 wins, 0 draws, and 1 loss at Gillette Stadium, accumulating 21 points. Historically, the Revolution have dominated Houston at home, winning their last five encounters and conceding only one goal. Houston Dynamo, despite a recent five-game unbeaten streak, has an underwhelming away record of three wins and four losses in eight road games, compounded by the absence of key defender Antonio Carlos due to injury. These factors strongly favor a New England victory at home.

The head-to-head matchups between New England and Houston frequently result in high-scoring affairs, with three of their last three competitive meetings seeing between three and six goals. Furthermore, 60% of their overall head-to-head games have surpassed 2.5 goals. New England's home games this season have also shown a propensity for goals, with 7 out of their last 10 home matches going over 2.5 goals, while averaging 2.10 goals scored per game. Houston's defensive solidity on the road is further compromised by the injury to Antonio Carlos, suggesting a higher likelihood of goals conceded.
